chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

You say during the ghusl of Friday: “O Allah, purify my heart from every affliction by which my religion is effaced and my deeds are nullified.” And you say during the ghusl of janabah: “O Allah, purify my heart, purify my deeds, accept my striving, and make what is with You better for me.”

key_terms.دِينِي: my religion, meaning one's faith and religious state
key_terms.سَعْيِي: my striving, effort, and devotional exertion
key_terms.طَهِّرْ قَلْبِي: purify my heart from inner corruption and spiritual defilement
key_terms.عَمَلِي: my deeds, meaning one's acts of worship and obedience
key_terms.غُسْلِ ٱلْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath performed to remove the state of janabah
key_terms.غُسْلِ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ: the ritual bath performed for Friday

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited during ghusl al-jumu'ah and ghusl al-janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits supplications to be recited during the ghusl of Friday and the ghusl of janabah. It emphasizes that ritual purification is joined with seeking inward purification, acceptance of deeds, and spiritual well-being from Allah.
